_comment: ISC-299's worker: it calls tools ENTHUSIASTICALLY and the filesystem refuses the writes. Taken from a measured run, not invented — container-live's first Linux CI execution of the whole chain on 2026-08-25 saw 17 native tool calls of which 11 failed with EACCES on /workspace/add.js, wrote nothing, and settled `success`. THE MIX IS THE POINT AND MUST NOT BE SIMPLIFIED TO ALL-ERRORS: the reads succeed here exactly as they did there, so a predicate of 'every call errored' passes this fixture happily and closes nothing. That is why the criterion turns on the TREE and not on the error ratio. The ISC-108 detector cannot catch this either — it asks whether tools were CALLED, and five are. The delay before turn_end is a WINDOW, not decoration: the paired test writes into the worktree during it to show the same fixture settles `success` once real work lands, so neither test can pass by the fixture merely being unusual.
